text:
Incident Bot: Paging: elevated latency on /v1/generate (p95 > 1.2s, baseline ~320ms). Detected 10% user errors and rising queue depth. Auto-escalation to on-call.

Maya Chen: acked. I'm on call. setting incident P1 and starting timeline. @Kai, can you join for infra traces?

Samir Patel: seeing p50 shifted from 180ms -> 450ms and p95 from 320ms -> 1.25s across hosted region us-east-1. Increase correlated with traffic spike + some infra churn. Affected: dedicated clusters on pool-a, small percentage of HTTPS requests getting 503s.

Jordyn Li: any recent infra changes? I see a rollout job for kernel-6.2.8 to pool-a around 10:05 (DeployBot noted).

DeployBot: deploy: kernel-6.2.8 -> pool-a (batch=25%) started at 2026-03-15T10:05:12Z by infra/auto-rolling. job_id=rb-20260315-001

Kai Park: on it. pulling perf counters and runqueue stats. attaching quick samples.

Kai Park: ```
# from host gpu-az1-12
perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,cpu-clock -I 1000 sleep 2
# sample
# 1000 ms: context-switches 23800, cpu-migrations 120, cpu-clock 1.02s
# runqueue length (procstat): runq-sz p95=7.8 (normal <1.5)
```

Lin Gomez: traces from the runtime show a cluster of spans at kernel_dispatch taking 400-900ms. Example span tree (shortened):
```
root: request /v1/generate (total=1300ms)
  ├─ routing (10ms)
  ├─ model_inference (950ms)
  │   ├─ kv_cache_lookup (5ms)
  │   ├─ kernel_dispatch (650ms)
  │   └─ postproc (270ms)
  └─ http_write (300ms)
```

Maya Chen: summary for customers: some queries to hosted API see large tail latencies; errors are low but tail latency causing user timeouts. Will open customer-facing status: "degraded performance".

Samir Patel: hypothesis list (working):
• H1: kernel rollout changed scheduler/hz behaviour -> higher runqueue -> kernel_dispatch tail latency spike.
• H2: a batching change in runtime increased head-of-line blocking for small requests under high concurrency.
• H3: transient NVidia driver/firmware issue on a subset of GPUs -> stalls.

Jordyn Li: evidence for H1: rollout started at 10:05 and p95 rose at ~10:07. Ops metrics show runqueue p99 jump. Evidence for H2: some traces show one request holding the worker for 250ms in pre-scheduling. Need allocators/queue lengths.

Kai Park: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause kernel rollout to remaining hosts, 2) rollback kernel on pool-a batch if correlation remains, 3) route new traffic away from pool-a to pool-b, 4) increase replicas for hot routes. I'll run 1 & 3 now.

Kai Park: `infra rollback rb-20260315-001 --target pool-a --batch 25%` (planning dry-run).

OpsBot: action: paused rollout rb-20260315-001 at 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z by infra/auto-rolling.

Maya Chen: @Lin, @Samir please prepare a quick delta trace set: capture 50 traces from before rollout (10:00-10:04) and 50 traces after (10:07-10:11). Put in shared s3 bucket and paste link. Also add perf counters from affected hosts.

Lin Gomez: uploaded traces: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3276543210/traces-after.tar.gz (10:07-10:15) and traces-before.tar.gz (10:00-10:04).

Samir Patel: uploaded perf snapshots and runqueue histograms: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3276543210/perf-snapshots.tar.gz

Jordyn Li: doing traffic reroute now: `routerctl shift --from pool-a --to pool-b --pct 60 --route /v1/generate`

DeployBot: routerctl: routing change initiated by Jordyn Li at 2026-03-15T10:18:45Z.

Maya Chen: customer comms drafted and posted to status page. Notifying top 5 customers with dedicated clusters.

Kai Park: after shift, p95 on /v1/generate dropped to ~420ms in pool-b. pool-a still shows tail spikes. This keeps H1 as leading hypothesis.

Samir Patel: added perf counter snippet showing scheduler latencies (per-cpu runqueue wait):
```
# host gpu-az1-12 runq wait micros (sample p95)
cpu0  180us
cpu1  260us
cpu2  720us
cpu3  410us
# some cpus showing >500us, correlates with kernel_dispatch delay
```

Jordyn Li: NVidia driver checks: no driver rollouts in timeframe; driver versions consistent across pool-a and pool-b. GPU error counters are nominal. Low probability for H3 but keep monitoring.

Maya Chen: tracking hypotheses and owners inline: 
- H1 (kernel scheduler change) — owner: Kai Park — evidence: temporal correlation, runqueue p99 jump, rollback reduces tail.
- H2 (runtime batching) — owner: Lin Gomez — evidence: some traces show head-of-line holds; need to reproduce under load.
- H3 (GPU/driver) — owner: Jordyn Li — evidence: none so far; deprioritized.

Kai Park: recommended remediation: roll back kernel on affected hosts in pool-a, then run canary subset with synthetic load and measure runqueue and span latencies. I'll schedule rollback batch now.

Kai Park: `infra rollback rb-20260315-001 --target pool-a --batch 25% --confirm` executed at 2026-03-15T10:25:12Z. Rolling back first batch.

OpsBot: rollback completed for batch-1 at 2026-03-15T10:27:34Z. Hosts returned to kernel-6.2.7.

Samir Patel: after rollback batch-1, p95 in pool-a decreased from 1.1s->520ms for affected hosts. Still above baseline, but trending down. Good signal.

Lin Gomez: will run a controlled batching disable in runtime on a few canary workers to validate H2. `runtimectl set batching.enabled=false --host canary-1`

Maya Chen: timeline (concise):
- 10:05:12 DeployBot started kernel-6.2.8 rollout to pool-a
- 10:07:10 latency p95 increases observed on /v1/generate
- 10:12:03 rollout paused (OpsBot)
- 10:18:45 traffic shift started away from pool-a (routerctl)
- 10:25:12 rollback batch-1 executed
- 10:27:34 rollback batch-1 completed; p95 improved on canaries

Samir Patel: next actions: collect heap of traces/perf for RCA, run prober to validate across all pools, get full host list that saw kernel update.

Jordyn Li: I'll export the host list and timestamped deploy events and drop into incident folder.

Kai Park: handing off live mitigation to night on-call @Kai (staying on case until metrics stable). Will own rollback sequence and final RCA writeup with Lin and Samir.

Maya Chen: thanks all. I've created the incident ticket and RCA placeholder: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INC-2026-327654 (please add notes). Handoff: continuing monitoring, if p95 < 400ms for 30m we'll mark mitigated.

Samir Patel: adding a TODO: run `perf record` on 3 affected hosts during synthetic load to capture kernel stacks (`perf record -a -g -- sleep 30`) and upload. Owner: Samir.

Lin Gomez: copying notes to thread and will start a small test disabling batching to see if head-of-line goes away.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-2026-327654 status updated: mitigations applied (rollback, routing), monitoring.

Maya Chen: closing live coordination. We'll reconvene for post-incident RCA at 14:30 with owners Kai (kernel), Lin (runtime), Samir (perf).

(End of thread)
